problem: Winkler's own 1886 account, as translated, dates the find of the ore to summer 1885 at the Himmelsfürst Fundgrube and says A. Weisbach recognised it as a new species and named it argyrodite. It also says the most careful analysis always showed a loss of 6 to 7 per cent.

fix.digest: In the summer of 1885 a rich silver ore of unusual appearance was raised at the Himmelsfürst mine near Freiberg. The mineralogist A. Weisbach recognised it as a new species and named it argyrodite. Winkler's careful analysis found silver, sulphur and traces of other metals, but the total always fell 6 to 7 per cent short. No account by the miners themselves was found.
